code: NOT A BLOW-UP: the survey's '876 m up' was the specimen standing at the WORLD ORIGIN (box top 876.35 above floor 144 = world y 0.35). It happened whenever floor 144 had been the paused preview below floor 143 first - exactly the survey runs that visited 143 just before 144 - and never on a direct arrival. 'Comes and goes' was visit order, not chance.

CAUSE (Godot 4.6 source): floor residency pauses a floor with PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED; a SoftBody3D with the default DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE then leaves Jolt, and on ENABLED Jolt rebuilds it from mesh_surface_get_arrays of its render mesh (_create_shared_settings). A body never drawn rebuilds at the mesh's own coordinates (the origin); the placement transform submitted at build is lost. Floor_content builds the floor below one work per frame while it is already paused, so its soft bodies left Jolt at mount INHERIT before the residency ever saw them; soft_mushrooms and revolving_joy_ride then pinned by call_deferred against those removed points and dragged their caps to the origin every frame (bodies 856 m long).

FIX, commons/void/floor_residency.gd only: each soft body's solver points are kept at pause and put back after the rebuild; a soft body born under the preview floor stays in the solver (KEEP_ACTIVE) until a frame-end hold after the work's own deferred setup, then leaves it as before (REMOVE), so a paused body still costs nothing per frame (freezing with KEEP_ACTIVE + pins was measured instead: ~20 us per body per frame, forever). The scene, its physics settings and the lesson path are unchanged.

RATES, 20 s per run: standalone scene 0/60 before (60 and 90 Hz, lesson, adapter, plain) - the scene itself never blew up; through the residency headless 20/20 stranded before, 0/30 after (60, 90 Hz, a Point Zero cube at the origin). Tower floor 144 walked down from 143: 14/14 stranded before (60 + 90 Hz, first arrivals and returns), 0/26 after; direct arrivals 0/13 before, 0/12 after and identical. Floors 139-146 walked down: 127 of 127 soft bodies off their floor before, 3 after, none from pausing (jelly_variants' ball falls through its slab on a fresh build too; softstopscene freezes its own spheres by disabling them). No NaN, no rigid body moved.

STILL OPEN, not changed: a floor LEFT and RETURNED TO rebuilds a drawn body from its last drawn pose, which becomes its rest shape - the specimen goes 0.61 -> 0.28 m tall over nine returns (0.49 -> 0.16 m on direct arrivals, the same before and after). Also: headless soft bodies are not the game's - under the dummy renderer the specimen settles 0.63 m tall, under a real renderer 0.48 m; and the 'table floating 1.8 m' in a standalone capture is the scene's original drop-test harness height kept for non-lesson placements (bench at y=3, harness box top 0.32); lesson:true (the tower's config) stands the legs on y=0.

code: NOT A THIN-SLAB TUNNEL AT REST. On floor 139 BouncyBall left the floor on every arrival (-1527 to -270 m after 20 s), WaterBalloon on most, and JellyCube either fell or ended as a flat sheet 0.000 m tall. None was resting and slipping through: the ball inflated from 0.28 to 0.71 m tall in 0.13 s and threw itself 3.8 m up; the balloon pancaked and its points came out of the slab's underside at exactly -0.36 m (the slab's thickness). The same scene on a bench slab, and on its own 4 cm pedestals with no slab, lost the same bodies, so it was the work, not the tower.

CAUSE: Jolt joins soft-body points only where mesh vertices are bit-identical, and BoxMesh builds each face's edge vertices on its own. At 0.25 m/4 subdivisions (JellyCube) and 0.20 and 0.22 m/5 (BouncyBall, WaterBalloon) neighbouring faces disagree by 1.3e-8 m: 52-63 OPEN SEAMS, so pressure pushes the faces apart and the body tears, launches itself or turns inside out flat. SlimePuddle (0.28/4) and QueerMorph (0.25/6) have 8 split points and always held; the 0.3 m default has none. Census: 315 of 864 cube BoxMesh configs (0.05-1.00 m x 0-8 subdivisions) have open seams, none at 0-3 subdivisions; SphereMesh, CapsuleMesh and CylinderMesh have none.

Settings swept on the bench before the seams were counted, each on its own: pressure halved, damping 0.08, stiffness 0.8 still lost or exploded a body; subdivisions 6 rescued two variants and blew WaterBalloon to 88 km (74 open seams); mass 4 and pressure 0 held all five but squashed them or took the pressure away. No setting fixes an open seam.

FIX, jelly_cube.gd only: _welded() snaps every BoxMesh vertex to the first one within 10 um before the mesh goes to the SoftBody3D, so each seam is one point. Vertex order is kept (the crown anchor's index still names its point), and a mesh with no split seam comes back bit-identical. jelly_variants.tscn and every authored number are unchanged; the five now stand as jellies 0.23-0.27 m tall (slime 0.11-0.15) where three were shards.

RATES, tower floor 139, 20 s per walk after arrival, every soft body on the floor (7: the five variants, the crown jelly_cube, softmill's sphere) against the band slab -0.25 m .. +5.5 m, windowed gl_compatibility: BEFORE 10 of 10 walks lost a body, 19 of 70 bodies out (BouncyBall 10/10, WaterBalloon 6/10, JellyCube 3/10, and flat in 5 more); AFTER 0 of 20 walks, 0 of 140 bodies, no NaN. Both runs mixed direct arrivals and walks down from 138 (the paused preview first) at 60 and 90 Hz. The crown jelly_cube (0.3 m, no split seam) and the softmill sphere measured the same before and after. Bench (scene on a 12.8 x 0.36 m slab and with no slab, 60 and 90 Hz): 2-3 of 5 lost before in every case, 0 of 5 after in all four.

code: fracture_model export, default 'tips' (the default was the fault): the original rule ('flood', kept) had no limit on a crack - every cracked cell pushed stress into all eight neighbours and every stressed cell cracked with at least 8 % a step, so within seconds every interior cell had cracked and the work stood as a solid orange plate (floor 116 showed exactly that)

tips: a crack is a tip that runs along its heading until it meets another crack (a T-junction) or the edge, sometimes splitting (branch_chance); a crack relieves a disc of stress (relief_radius / relief_strength), so the next nucleates where the plate is still loaded; the far-field load rises to load_max, so the network refines in generations - primaries widest and coolest, the cracks between them thinner, fresh tips pale; cycle + hold_seconds then a fresh plate (it never ran again once settled)

cost: nucleation scan only when an upper bound says a crack can start (0.16 ms a step), relief disc precomputed, settled quads frozen and the mesh rebuilt at 5 Hz (0.8 ms); crack quads cast no shadow; config keys fracture_model / seed / cycle

colours: every update writes a colour per cell and the material never read them - all twelve systems stood as white spheres; vertex_color_use_as_albedo

each system restarts from its seeds when the cycle comes round to it (they stayed saturated at their caps for good); parked cells at scale 0 (8000 at 1 % drew a lattice of specks)
